Biography

The short version

I am a freelance videographer and editor based in Manchester, working across the UK for brands, agencies and event teams. Ten years on set — four of them as an editor before I picked up a camera full time — means I cut for the story first and shoot with the timeline already in my head.

That editing background changes how I work on a shoot day. I know which angles a sequence will actually need, so we capture coverage that cuts together instead of a pile of beautiful shots that do not join up. It is the difference between a two-day edit and a two-week one.

I run a compact, self-sufficient kit: camera, sound, lighting and a mobile edit station, so a small production does not need a van full of crew. For bigger jobs I bring in the same trusted team I have worked with for years.

Mission

What I care about

Three principles that decide how every project runs — and which ones I turn down.

01

The edit decides everything

Shooting is only half the job. I storyboard the sequence before the day so we capture what the cut will need.

02

Deadlines are part of the craft

A film that lands after the campaign has moved on is worthless. Rough cuts go out within 48 hours, every time.

03

Honest about scope

If the budget cannot deliver the idea, I say so before we start rather than quietly cutting corners later.

Timeline

How I got here

  1. 2015

    Started as an editor

    Cut corporate and music content in a Manchester post house for four years before taking on camera work.

  2. 2019

    Went freelance

    Moved into a combined shooter-editor role, which immediately shortened every project timeline.

  3. 2022

    First retainers

    Signed the first monthly content clients, moving from one-off films to ongoing production.

  4. 2025

    Hart & Grain

    Formed a small collective of trusted crew for larger productions while staying the single point of contact.
